definitions.text: a diphthong, employed in the Latin language, and thence in the English language, as the representative of the Greek diphthong oe. In many words in common use, e alone stands instead of oe. Classicists prefer to write the diphthong oe separate in Latin words.
The colorless porous framework, or stroma, of red blood corpuscles from which the zooid, or hemoglobin and other substances of the corpuscles, may be dissolved out.
The various relations of animals and plants to one another and to the outer world.
See Economical.
See Economics.
See Economy.
See Ecumenical.
A swelling from effusion of watery fluid in the cellular tissue beneath the skin or mucous membrance; dropsy of the subcutaneous cellular tissue. [Written also edema.]
Pertaining to, or of the nature of, edema; affected with edema.
A circular or oval window; -- generally used of architecture of the 17th and 18th centuries. A famous room in the palace of Versailles bears this name, from the oval window opening into it.
(Ornamental Art) Characterized by, or decorated with, small round points, spots, or rings; as, oil-de-perdrix pattern.
Having a brownish red color; -- used esp. of light-colored red wine.
A glance of the eye; an amorous look. [Obs.] She gave strange oeillades and most speaking looks. Shak.
An eye, bud, or shoot, as of a plant; an oilet. [Obs.] Holland.
A salt of the supposed oenanthic acid.

Having, or imparting, the odor characteristic of the bouquet of wine; specifically used, formerly, to designate an acid whose ethereal salts were supposed to occasion the peculiar bouquet, or aroma, of old wine. Cf. OEnanthylic. OEnanthic acid, an acid obtained from oenanthic ether by the action of alkalies. the bouquet, or aroma, of wine) found in wine lees, and consisting of a complex mixture of the ethereal salts of several of the higher acids of the acetic acid series. It has an ethereal odor, and it used in flavoring artificial wines and liquors. Called also oil of wine. See Essential oil, under Essential.
An oily substance obtained by the distillation of castor oil, recognized as the aldehyde of oenanthylic acid, and hence called also oenanthaldehyde.
The ketone of oenanthic acid.
A hydrocarbon radical formerly supposed to exist in oenanthic acid, now known to be identical with heptyl.
A salt of oenanthylic acid; as, potassium oenanthylate.

Pertaining to, derived from, or containing, oenanthyl; specifically, designating an acid formerly supposed to be identical with the acid in oenanthic ether, but now known to be identical with heptoic acid.
A colorless liquid hydrocarbon, having a garlic odor; heptine.
Of, pertaining to, or designating, an acid formerly supposed to be the acid of oenanthylic ether, but now known to be a mixture of higher acids, especially capric acid. [Obs.]
The coloring matter of red wines.
Knowledge of wine, scientific or practical.
Wine mixed with honey; mead, [R.]
See Alcoholometer.
A lover of wine. [R.] Thackeray.
Pertaining to an acid now called sulphovinic, or ethyl sulphuric, acid.

The C.G.S. unit of magnetic reluctance or resistance, equal to the reluctance of a centimeter cube of air (or vacuum) between parallel faces. Also, a reluctance in which unit magnetomotive force sets up unit flux.
Same as Esophagus, Esophageal, etc.
Of or pertaining to the gadflies.
A gadfly.
Of or pertaining to sexual desire; -- mostly applied to brute animals; as, the oestrual period; oestrual influence.
The state of being under oestrual influence, or of having sexual desire.
(Zoöl.)
A genus of gadflies. The species which deposits its larvæ in the nasal cavities of sheep is oestrus ovis.
A vehement desire; esp. (Physiol.), the periodical sexual impulse of animals; heat; rut.
